sentences.text:
This Petition, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Order Was Made Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr Justice S.R.Krishna Kumar
 Oral Order

In this petition, petitioner seeks quashing of proceedings in C.C.No.10953/2021 for the offence
punishable under Sections 418, 420 read with Section 34 of Ipc and Section 23 of Karnataka
Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 1999 on the file of Addl. Civil Judge and Jmfc, Kunigal.

2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent and perused the material on record.
3.
Respondent No.2 having been served with notice of the petition, has chosen to remain unrepresented and has not contested the petition.
4. A perusal of the material on record will indicate that it is an undisputed fact that the petitioner is working as Panchayat Development Officer in Kaggere Gram Panchayat since 2012.

Pursuant to a private complaint submitted by respondent No.2 against the petitioner and Lakshmamma, the matter was referred to jurisdictional Police authorities for investigation culminating in charge sheet and C.C.No.83/2016, which is pending before the learned Magistrate.

5. It is the case of the petitioner that since he is a public servant, necessary sanction by State Government ought to have been obtained under Section 197 of Cr.P.C. before the Magistrate took cognizance of the offence as against the petitioner and on this ground the impugned proceedings Sri Chandrahasa S L vs State Of Karnataka on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106885546/
2 qua petitioner/accused No.2 deserves to be quashed.

entities.text: Sri Chandrahasa S L vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is also submitted that even subsequently,
sanction is not obtained by the Police authorities, even till today though charge sheet is filed as long back as on 24.08.2016.

It is also submitted that a perusal of the allegations made in the private complaint, statement of witness, documents and charge sheet do not disclose that the petitioner is guilty of any of the offences alleged against him.

It is therefore, submitted that on this ground also,
the impugned proceedings qua the petitioner deserves to be quashed.

Further, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that irregularities pointed out by respondent No.2-complainant have been subsequently rectified as evident from the material on record, in particular, the communication dated 24.10.2015.
It is therefore submitted that the impugned proceedings qua the petitioner deserves to be quashed.

7. As rightly contended by learned counsel for the petitioner, material on record discloses that prior/previous sanction by the State Government has not been obtained before the Magistrate took cognizance of the offences qua the petitioner who is undisputedly public servant as required under Section 197 of Cr.P.C, and consequently, the impugned proceedings for want/lack of sanction deserves to be quashed.
8.

In addition thereto material on record also indicates that apart from the fact that the irregularities/defect have been subsequently rectified the contents of the private complaint,
statement of witness, documents and charge sheet do not make out commission of any offences by the petitioner under Section 23 of Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 1999 or NC:
2025:KHC:665 under Sections 418, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC and on this ground also, the impugned proceedings deserves to be quashed.
9.

entities.text: Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 1999 or NC:
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The petition is hereby allowed.
ii) The proceedings in C.C.No.10953/2021 for the offence punishable under Sections 418, 420 read with Section 34 of IPC and Section 23 of Karnataka Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 1999 on the file of Addl.
Civil Judge and JMFC, Kunigal qua the petitioner are hereby quashed.
Sd/-
(S.R.KRISHNA KUMAR) JUDGE MDS Sri Chandrahasa S L vs State Of Karnataka on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106885546/
